newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks open higher, BHP and banks lead.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks open higher, BHP and banks lead.

text.p: Australian shares opened firmer on Monday, led by gains in the banking and resource sector as investors remained optimistic that the Reserve Bank would cut interest rates soon and as a result of stronger metal prices.
"It's looking relatively strong, mainly on the back of commodity prices and the possibility of a rate cut in the next week or two," Peter Struk of Reynolds & Co said.
The All Ordinaries index had gained 19.6 points to 2,710.8 at 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT).
Stronger base metal prices pulled the Broken Hill Pty Ltd 24 cents or 1.3 percent higher to A$18.24 (US$13.45) and WMC 18 cents up to A$7.92.
Rio Tinto again failed to follow the market higher as its London listing weakened on Friday.
The banking sector gained almost one percent in early trade.

"The banks are up purely on the prospect of a rate cut," one dealer said, adding players remained confident the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) would announce another interest rate cut sometime after its next meeting on August 5.
Westpac jumped 22 cents to A$8.45 in active trade.

Both Westpac and Bank of Melbourne moved into record territory on Friday when Australian authorities finally cleared Westpac's bid for the regional bank after months of deliberations. Bank of Melbourne was steady at A$9.80 in morning trade.
In the wake of the approval, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said it would look at any proposal by National Australia Bank to take over St George Bank on its merits.
National Australia Bank climbed 24 cents to A$19.52, while St George firmed 20 to A$8.73.
Taking Friday's gains into account, NAB has now recovered all of its losses on Thursday when the bank reported lower than expected third quarter net profits.
"They knocked (NAB) down too far on Thursday and are now moving back up again," Peter Struk said.

G.E. Crane gained 10 cents to A$13.40 after the metal distribution and building products supplier reported a 41 percent rise in year net profit to A$28.94 million, and said it expected local business conditions to improve i coming months.
Among weaker stocks, ICI Australia fell 12 cents to A$13.13 as investors took home profits after Friday's gains.

Investment and manufacturing firm Austrim jumped 25 cents to a record A$4.05 after it reported a near five-times jump in full-year profits, and said it expected further growth in the current financial year.
It also announced a two-for-five rights issue to raise A$208 million to reduce debt and for additional working capital.
Improving gold bullion prices helped the gold stocks index rise 1.7 percent. Heavyweight Normandy Mining firmed four cents to A$1.52.
News Corp rose two cents to A$6.81, while Australis Media shares were suspended at the company's request.
The suspension was made to give the market time to absorb Friday's announcement of a proposed merger between pay-TV operators Australis and Foxtel, jointly owned by News Corp and state-owned Telstra.
